verdict: Red 7/10 (labelled ACCEPT-WITH-CUTS but its actual instruction is FLAT and cancel the pre-print court), blue 8/10 PARTIALLY OVERTURNED, and all three documents converge on FLAT into the 2026-08-13 BMO print. The reason this escalates is not disagreement about today - it is that the post-print gate both benches wrote can fire into a STARTER within days, and it is explicitly conditioned on a verification NEITHER bench could execute. Red's decisive contribution is that the court's reason to exist was doubly false. First, the defense's centerpiece that the FY guide is 'arithmetically near-dead' fails a seasonality check it never ran: 2025 printed $11.8M at 58.8% GM, $24.55M at 61.2%, $6.28M at 44.4%, then $48.28M at 61.4% with +$5.98M of operating income - Q4 was 53% of the year and quarter-to-quarter swings ran 2.1x to 7.7x. The guide requires mean reversion in a lumpy delivery model, not a miracle, and management introduced the negative-mid-to-high-teens EBITDA guide at Q1 already knowing Q1's -$12.8M. Blue reduced this from FATAL to SIZING-grade on a fair point: red's kill rests on the untested premise that Q1's 26.6% gross margin is transient mix rather than structural drone-ASP pressure, and red's own change-my-mind list concedes that is unestablished - while the sentinel2 read cuts against easy capacity for a 3.6x ramp. Second, the claim that the bear arithmetic is 'unpriced' is refuted: 3.51M shares short is 20.29% of a 17.30M float with 7.37 days to cover. Blue sustained this exactly and added the right qualifier - three analysts is not efficient pricing, so red proved CROWDED, not PRICED. That kills both the short (squeeze fuel, per the conditioning doctrine) and the pre-print court, without establishing fair value. The governance finding is the most durable output. The September-2025 follow-on was priced 2025-09-11, about day 90 of a 180-day IPO lockup (waiver implied), and the company used its own cash to repurchase shares from existing holders at $18.50. Blue corrected the count upward from primary - 1,116,312 shares under a 2025-09-07 Stock Repurchase Agreement, roughly $19.6M of company cash, with New Generation Aerospace separately selling $7.05M - against a stock at $8.44 eleven months later. Management facilitated an insider exit at 2.2x today's price. Blue's sharpest new finding ties the two sides together: the September raise netted about $63M after the repurchase and $54.2M remained at 3/31, roughly four quarters, so red's 'squeeze fuel' and its dilution finding are the same event - a post-print squeeze is precisely management's demonstrated sell-into-strength window, which caps the long tail too. What survives is a symmetric no-trade: long blocked by guide-cut risk plus the demonstrated issuance reflex, short blocked by 20% short interest and 7.4 days to cover, and a tape already +47.8% off the $5.71 low. Both benches agree the pre-print court should be cancelled outright rather than time-boxed, since a court cannot add sizing value racing a two-day catalyst. Blue's post-print gate is GM >=40% with the guide intact implies a STARTER - but only after checking for a live shelf or ATM, and that check has never been run. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: blue's STARTER gate (GM>=40% at the 8/13 BMO print) is VOID unless the shelf/ATM cap-structure pull executes first (pull-cap-structure-in-primary-DD is a standing rule; no bench ran it — sec.gov 403). Gate does not fire on an unverified cap table. KILL for now; pack carries the precondition.
